# Laboratory for Atmospheric and Space Physics (LASP)

## Snapshot

| | |
|---|---|
| **Country** | United States |
| **City** | Boulder, CO |
| **Tier** | Emerging / conference-affiliated (Tier IV) |
| **Primary ecosystem** | Metrology / remote sensing — flagged |
| **Publicly linked people** | Julian Gieseler |
| **Flag** | IR-EMPOWER talk was on **apparent emissivity of semitransparent samples at PTB** — the evidenced instrumentation is PTB's |

## Why it matters — and why it is flagged

LASP enters the map through participant affiliation: the IR-EMPOWER talk
was explicitly about **apparent emissivity of semitransparent samples at
PTB**, so the emissivity instrumentation evidenced in the public record
is mainly PTB's. LASP is therefore flagged as a **conference-affiliated
contributor** rather than a primary emissivity institution on the same
footing as PTB or CEMHTI. Retained for completeness.

## Scope of activity (as evidenced publicly)

### Methodology

Conference-affiliated contributor; talk was on apparent emissivity of
semitransparent samples at PTB. The visible scientific link runs through
collaboration with PTB's emissivity infrastructure rather than through
LASP-hosted emissivity facilities.

### Application domains

- Atmospheric and space physics

## IR-EMPOWER contributions

- **Julian Gieseler** — apparent emissivity of semitransparent samples
  at PTB.

## Why LASP is retained

The map deliberately tolerates a small "flagged" tier for entities whose
IR-EMPOWER participation is documented but whose public institutional
pages do not currently surface emissivity as a program. Including them
keeps the record honest: it distinguishes institutions with dedicated
facilities from institutions whose visible contribution, at this point,
is a specific piece of collaborative work carried out at someone else's
facility. LASP is an example of the latter category.
